Subject: Signature ownership and last-mile handoff for MSA + Order Form

Team — looping you both in to move this across the finish line. Attached are the redlines we received back from Acme (Redlined_MSA_v3.pdf) and the final Order Form draft (OrderForm_Acme_20280601.docx). Highlights:
- All commercial redlines accepted except the two POA/authority items called out by Acme legal (see pages 2–3 of the redline).
- We agreed internally to our standard warranty/indemnity language; Acme accepted with one small edit to Section 9 (privacy carve-out).

Immediate asks: 
1) Laura — can you confirm the signatory evidence we need on file for Acme’s VP Finance? Laura suggested a signer authority letter + corporate resolution; please confirm exactly which pieces will satisfy our legal/compliance team.
2) Monica — once we have signer names/roles confirmed, who on your side will own the DocuSign envelope from Redwood? We need one envelope owner at Redwoods and an envelope owner at Acme for audit trail.
3) Claire / Procurement (Acme) — please confirm the signing order on your end and whether your procurement team will initiate the DocuSign envelope from Acme’s account or want Redwood to initiate. If you can attach Acme’s signatory list, that speeds the process.

Goal: envelope in flight by EOD Monday (Jun 4). Final clean PDF post-signature should be routed to legal-archive@redwood.com and the customer success owner.

Thanks —
Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: OrderForm_Acme_20280601.docx (docx, 45KB)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Signature ownership and last-mile handoff for MSA + Order Form

Jonas — thanks, reviewing now. Quick summary from legal: 
- Signer authority: we will need (a) a dated signatory authorization letter on Acme letterhead that names the signatory and the position, and (b) a copy of either the board resolution OR the corporate registry extract showing signatory authority. One of those paired items satisfies our records policy.
- Witness/notarization: not required for US-based signers, but if Acme uses an APAC signatory we need notarization or local equivalent.
- DocuSign envelope ownership: fine for Redwood to initiate (preferred) so we can ensure the correct signing order and attach the clean final copy in envelope history. If Acme insists on their envelope we need the envelope ID and access to the audit log post-signature.

I am attaching a short checklist we use for sign-off — it speeds routing if Acme supplies the items on the list before sending. Also flagging a one-line redline in Section 7 (data retention) that I see was nudged by Acme; we accepted their language but want a clean copy showing the final agreed text before executing.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Signer_Authority_Checklist.pdf (pdf, 75KB)]

From: Claire Rivers <claire.rivers@acme.com>

Thanks Jonas — Acme can confirm the signing plan. Summary from our side:
- Signatories: Michael Fong (SVP Finance) will sign for Acme. He has authority up to $50M per our charter; we will send a scanned signatory letter and a page from the corporate registry.
- Signing order: 1) Acme (Michael) 2) Redwood (authorized signer) — Acme prefers to receive the envelope so our finance team can track internally. If Redwood must initiate, we can transfer visibility on your audit logs.
- DocuSign: we are on DocuSign account acmecorp-prod (Account ID: 998877). Procurement will create the envelope unless Redwood prefers to create and then push ownership — Procurement can loop in support@docusign.com for any cross-account transfer.

Attached is the Acme signatory list for reference. I will push the signatory letter and registry excerpt to you by midday Monday.

Claire Rivers
Director, Procurement Operations
Acme Corp

Ben / Monica — per Claire, Acme prefers to originate the envelope from their DocuSign account (acmecorp-prod). That’s fine but we still need to do two things on our side: 
1) Redwood needs to confirm who will be the authorized Redwood signer in DocuSign and that person needs to be listed as the second signer in the sequence. Laura, can you confirm the exact Redwood signer (title and full legal name) we should use on the envelope?
2) Ben — once Acme creates the envelope, please request the envelope ID and the full DocuSign audit log. We will store the clean executed PDF and the audit log in legal-archive@redwood.com. Please also attach our Final_MSA_CleanCopy.pdf in the envelope as the version-of-record (if Acme will allow).

Ben — please coordinate with Claire’s procurement contact and confirm by EOD that we have envelope ownership or, if Acme owns it, that they will share the audit artifacts.

Thanks —
Jonas
